title: The Lion and the Mouse

full_text:
A mighty lion, weary from hunting across the sun-drenched savannah, lay sleeping peacefully beneath the sprawling shade of an ancient baobab tree. His massive golden mane rippled in the breeze, and his deep snores stirred the dust around his great paws.

A timid little field mouse, scurrying through the tall grass in search of seeds, did not notice the sleeping predator and inadvertently ran straight across the lion's broad nose.

Startled from his nap, the furious king of beasts struck out with lightning speed. His heavy paw clamped down upon the tiny creature, pinning her helpless against the hard ground. Opening his cavernous jaws, the lion prepared to crush the mouse in a single bite.

"Spare me, O King!" squeaked the terrified mouse, trembling in every whisker. "I meant no disrespect! I was running blindly from a hawk. Forgive my clumsy blunder! If you grant me my life, I promise that one day I will repay your royal mercy!"

The lion let out a roar of thunderous laughter that shook the surrounding acacia branches. "Repay me? A wretched, insignificant speck of fur repay the sovereign of the forest? What an absurd fancy!" Yet, amused by her sheer boldness, the lion lifted his paw and let the tiny creature scurry safely into the rocks.

A few days later, while patrolling his territory, the lion walked into a hunter's concealed trap. Strong hemp cords snapped tight around his limbs, hoisting him helpless into a heavy rope net. The mighty beast roared in fury and thrashing anguish, but every struggle only tightened the knots.

Hearing that familiar, desperate roar echoing through the ravines, the little mouse rushed to the scene. Without hesitation, she set her sharp, needle-like teeth against the thickest cord, gnawing with frantic determination until the fibers frayed and snapped. One by one, she severed the binding ropes until the great king stepped down, completely free.

Looking down at his tiny deliverer with humble reverence, the lion bowed his great head: "You were right, little friend. Today you have taught the King of the Forest that even the smallest heart can save the mighty."
moral: No act of kindness, however small, is ever wasted; little friends may prove great allies.

Believing rumors and flattery without proof
